ModelVariations.Description: Published factory material gives approximately 8 ft 6 in bridge clearance with radar mast down and about 13 ft with mast up.

ModelCharacter: A highly unconventional 8'6"-beam long-range cruiser designed to travel like a small commercial vessel rather than a yacht. The narrow hull, separated aft cockpit/pilothouse/forward cabin zones and single 85 hp diesel deliver 7–9-knot economy, easy slip access and potential legal-width road transport.
DesignLineage: SeaPiper developed the 35 as a deliberately narrow, affordable long-range cruiser rather than a scaled-down conventional trawler.
The design uses an 8'6" beam, roughly 36-foot hull and single Beta Marine diesel.
A folding mast reduces bridge clearance to roughly 8'6" for inland-route flexibility.
The model's industrial aesthetic and separated living zones are intentional design choices, not evidence of unfinished yacht styling.
OwnershipCharacter: Mechanically simple, economical and unusually easy to berth for its length. The narrow beam reduces interior openness, while unusual construction details, limited production and proprietary finish work can require owner ingenuity.

Strengths: High interior volume for nominal length
Flybridge convertible layout

ModelVariations.Description: Tollycraft models commonly appeared with different gasoline/diesel packages and bridge layouts; individual equipment must be verified.

ModelCharacter: A quintessential Pacific Northwest family cruiser: solid-fiberglass modified-V hull, twin inboards, lower helm, roomy two-stateroom interior and a practical cockpit/flybridge arrangement designed for year-round coastal use rather than trawler-speed economy.
DesignLineage: The 34 Sport Sedan was produced from 1987–1993.
It is a later model than Tollycraft's earlier 34 Sedan and should not be conflated with the 1972–1980 generation.
Two flybridge arrangements were offered for different regional preferences: helm-aft for East Coast buyers and helm-forward for Pacific buyers.
Fuel capacity increased after the first production year, so 200- and 296-gallon specifications both legitimately appear.
OwnershipCharacter: Solid fiberglass construction and conventional twin inboards make the structure and machinery understandable, but twin engines, flybridge systems and aging fuel/electrical installations create normal 34-foot motor-yacht upkeep. Gas and diesel examples have materially different operating economics.
